simple.meaning: חֲשַׁח (chăshach) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to be necessary (from the idea of convenience) or (transitively) to need.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 2 times across Ezra, Daniel, beginning at Ezra 6:9. Its contexts include offering, kingship, priesthood.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חֲשַׁח (H2818).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: חֲשַׁח (chăshach) / H2818 is traced through Ezra 6:9, Daniel 3:16 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: to be necessary (from the idea of convenience) or (transitively) to need
definitions.full: H2818. chashach [ חֲשַׁח ] verb need (Assyrian —ašâ—u , crave ; Syriac in need of ; not ᵑ7 ; — Pe`al Participle plural חָֽשְׁחִין Dan 3:16 , singular Infinitive (van d. H., wrongly, ׳חַשׁ ). [ חַשְׁחָה ] noun feminine thing needed (Syriac ; Nö in K p. 175 ); — plural חַשְׁחָן Ezra 6:9 .
definitions.rootNote: (Aramaic) a collateral root to one corresponding to 2363 in the sense of readiness;
